name: OpenBot
tagline: A control room you run yourself, where each AI helper gets its own locked-down computer instead of the run of your machine.
sentence: Give one of its AI coworkers a job, and your own rules approve every click and file it touches before it happens, on its own sealed-off computer, with a plain record of what it did and why.
replaces: xAI's hosted Grok Bot, and similar hosted AI teammate products

board.say: Turning an AI helper loose on your browser and files is risky: one wrong click can hit the wrong website or the wrong file, and afterward it's hard to say exactly what it did.
board.eg: Most AI agent setups run right inside your own browser and file system, so a mistake there is a mistake on your real machine.

board.say: You start a conversation with one of your coworkers in its own channel, or a schedule starts it for you.
board.eg: Message it directly, or set it on a repeating schedule and it starts itself in that same channel at the time you picked.

board.say: A plain-language job, plus whichever tools you already decided that coworker may use.
board.eg: For example: a browser limited to your own company's sites, files it may read but not change, or a connection to Google Drive or Notion. Any agent that speaks AG-UI (an open standard for how an agent talks to its interface) can fill the coworker role, whatever framework built it.

board.say: It plans its next move and checks with your rules before doing anything.
steps: It decides what it wants to do next - open a page, click something, read or save a file
That plan goes to one gatekeeper first, which compares it against the rules you wrote
An allowed action runs on that coworker's own computer, its own browser and files, never yours, and gets written to a record before it happens
If it hits a login wall or a two-factor prompt, it stops and asks a person to take over
board.eg: Try it yourself: ask a coworker to open news.ycombinator.com and tell you the top story, then read the record of exactly what it did.

board.say: Work you can watch happen, and a record of exactly what happened.

outputs.what: Work carried out where you can watch it
outputs.eg: A live view of the coworker's own screen while it works, in its channel

outputs.what: A complete, readable record of every action
outputs.eg: A list of what was allowed, what was refused, and which rule caused it

outputs.what: A coworker you can safely hand real logins to
outputs.eg: Its browser, files and tool access all stay inside its own locked-down computer, not yours

before: Most AI agent setups run right inside your own browser and files, so one bad action is a mistake on your real machine.
It's hard to know exactly what an agent did after the fact, or to stop it before it does something you'd have refused.
Picking one agent framework to build on usually locks you into it.
after: Each coworker gets its own computer: its own browser, its own files, only the tools you specifically allow.
Every action is checked against your rules before it happens, and written to a record you can read afterward.
Any agent that speaks the same open connection standard can be a coworker here, so switching frameworks doesn't mean starting over.
uses_note: It's 41 days old and still alpha (an early, still-changing release). We found real coverage of its launch, but no independent, verified report yet of a team running it day to day - real use is still early.

steps: A developer clones [the repository](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot), copies `.env.example` to `.env`, and follows the README's [Quick start](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot#quick-start) to connect a free CopilotKit Intelligence project and add a model key.

Run `bash scripts/start.sh` to bring up the database, the API and the app, then watch the [demo video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/535ef7ee-1631-4a69-b839-564c56cf90b4) to see what a working setup looks like.
In your running copy, message a coworker to check a page online and report back, then read `/admin/audit` to see exactly what it did and why it was allowed.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot

If that scan passes: in a scratch folder, follow the README's Quick start with a throwaway OpenAI key and CopilotKit's free Intelligence plan, run `bash scripts/start.sh`, and ask the built-in coworker to open news.ycombinator.com and report the top story. Show me what it did and what /admin/audit recorded. 10 minutes max, then stop and report back in plain English.

best_for: You have a developer who can run Docker (a tool for packaging software to run the same way anywhere) and wants AI agents that can touch real tools without touching your production systems
You need to show your boss or an auditor exactly what an AI agent did and why it was allowed to
skip_if: You want something to sign up for today - this is a template you run and maintain yourself, not a hosted product
You're not comfortable running a database and a model API key (a code the AI provider issues you) yourself - there's real setup here

alternatives.name: Grok Bot (xAI)
alternatives.line: The closed, hosted product OpenBot's own launch post positioned itself against - AI teammates you subscribe to (through a SuperGrok or Cursor plan) rather than run and govern yourself.

alternatives.name: KiroCrew
alternatives.line: Another open-source way to run multiple AI agents, built for preserving context across sessions and scheduled work rather than OpenBot's per-agent sandboxing and audit trail.

watch: **A template, not a hosted product.** Nothing to sign up for - you clone it, configure it, and run and maintain it yourself.

**Alpha, and it needs more than its own free code.** It also needs a CopilotKit Intelligence project (a free plan exists, and you can run that part yourself too) for memory and lasting conversations - it isn't fully stand-alone yet.
**41 days old and moving fast.** 15 releases already, at v0.0.15 - expect breaking changes between versions.
**We found no independent report yet of a team actually running this day to day.** The coverage so far is about the launch, not about results.

footprint.disk: About **1.4 GB** for the container image itself (the app, the API and one coworker's browser together), per OpenBot's own measurement. Its docs recommend 4 GB free minimum, 8 GB so a coworker has room to save files.
footprint.memory: **409 MB** just idling, growing to about **550 MB** with one coworker's browser active (OpenBot's own measurement, on an Apple-chip machine). Its docs recommend at least 2 GB, 4 GB if several coworkers work at once.
footprint.runs_on: Mac, Windows or Linux with Docker (a tool for packaging software to run the same way anywhere) installed. Also needs Bun 1.3+ to build the app, a PostgreSQL database (or let OpenBot run one for you), a model API key (OpenAI, Anthropic or others - none is bundled), and a CopilotKit Intelligence project (a free plan exists, and it can be run on your own server too).
